newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Bayer AG buys stake in Brazil's CPB.
newsitem.headline: Bayer AG buys stake in Brazil's CPB.

text.p: German chemical giant Bayer AG bought a 66.67 percent stake in Brazilian plastics maker Central Polimeros da Bahia SA (CPB) for $51.6 million, Bayer officials said.

"We have moved into Brazil to get a leading position in Brazil and Latin America," Klaus Stoeger, general manager of Bayer's Plastics Business Group, told reporters at a news conference at CPB's plant in Camacari, near the city of Salvador in the northeastern state of Bahia.

CPB is a leading producer of ABS (acrylonitrite- butadine-styrene) plastics in Brazil. Through the acquisition of 66.67 percent of CPB capital stock, Bayer aims to become the leading supplier of ABS engineering plastic products to Brazil's burgeoning automobile and electronic equipment sectors.
CPB, which employs 200 people at its plant in Camacari posted sales last year of $65 million and enjoys a 50 percent share of Brazil's plastics market.
Theunis Marinho, the financial and administrative director of Bayer's Brazil unit, Bayer SA, has been named managing director of the new venture.
Marinho said the first objective is to double output at CPB to its capacity of 50,000 metric tonnes. He did not say how much the company would have to invest to reach its goal.
